title: Release engineering weekly notes - 2026-03-17
content:
Release Engineering - Weekly Meeting Notes
Date: 2026-03-17
Attendance: Ava Patel (chair), Maya Singh, Carlos Rivera, Priya Natarajan, Ethan Brooks, on-call: Samir Kaur (partial)

High-level summary:
- Prep for release train v1.42 scheduled for 2026-03-18 (mid-window deploy at 02:00 UTC). Primary focus: client-side batching improvements, kernel selection tweaks for int8 paths, and a set of smaller bugfixes.
- Hotfix HOTFIX-21 (memory leak in kv-cache eviction) was cut yesterday; canary went well in eu-west-1 but we saw a small error spike in us-east-1 during a specific traffic pattern. Root cause narrowed to request routing race (REL-1430).
- Canary metrics look acceptable overall, but we want an extra 2-hour canary in us-east-1 before full rollout.

Release train status (v1.42):
- Release lead: Maya Singh.
- Release branch: release/v1.42 (merged into main on 2026-03-16).
- Blockers: REL-1435 (telemetry schema mismatch) — mitigation: deploy schema migration job in read-only mode prior to main deploy. Owner: Carlos. Due: 2026-03-18 00:30 UTC.
- Critical PRs merged: #3412 (batch scheduling improvements), #3420 (runtime kernel fallback), #3427 (changelog updates).
- Smoke test plan: automated smoke + canary verification script (rel-canary-check) to run post-deploy. If p95 latency > +15% or error rate > 0.5% from baseline, rollback.

Hotfix update (HOTFIX-21):
- Purpose: mitigate kv-cache memory leak under high-concurrency prefix-fanout (customer report INF-2338).
- Canary: deployed to eu-west-1 (10% of traffic) on 2026-03-16 20:00 UTC. Metrics: no memory increase over 24h, error rate unchanged.
- us-east-1 canary observed 0.2% spike in grpc timeouts between 03:00-03:15 UTC correlated with routing GC event (REL-1430). Logged as follow-up; will add guard in router to avoid concurrent routing table rebuild + eviction.
- Decision: extend canary in us-east-1 until 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC and include additional synthetic load to reproduce.

Change log highlights (user-facing):
- API: improved batching heuristics to reduce small-batch latency by ~8-12% (PR #3412).
- Runtime: safer kernel fallback for int8 models to prevent OOM on long-seq requests (PR #3420).
- Fix: kv-cache eviction bug (HOTFIX-21) — customer-facing incidents should be resolved after full rollout.
- Note: no API contract changes. No client migrations required.

Canary & Observability:
- Canary dashboards to monitor: token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, grpc error rates, OOM occurrences, memory RSS by process.
- Baseline windows: last 7 days pre-canary. Canary checks integrated into CI (rel-canary-check pipeline).
- Observability gaps: missing per-route histogram for embedding requests (tracked REL-1438). Action: Priya to add histograms + Grafana panel. ETA 2026-03-22.

Incidents & roll-forward follow-ups:
- Incident: 2026-03-12 partial outage in us-west-2 (postmortem draft in Confluence). Root cause: autoscaler mis-evaluation with heterogeneous GPU types. Action items: tighten scaling policies (SRE).
- Postmortem action: Release team to include autoscaler stress test in pre-release checklist (owner: Ethan).

Operational notes / deployment windows:
- Primary release window: 02:00 - 06:00 UTC.
- Rollout plan: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 20-30 minute observation per step. Automatic rollback triggers enabled.
- Emergency rollback: use release/rollback tool with snapshot restore. Runbook: Release Playbook (linked).

Action items (owner, due):
- Carlos: run schema migration job in read-only mode and verify telemetry compatibility. Due 2026-03-18 00:30 UTC.
- Priya: add per-route embedding histograms + Grafana panel. Due 2026-03-22.
- Maya: lead canary in us-east-1 and capture synthetic load results. Due 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC.
- Ethan: add autoscaler stress test to pre-release checklist and add to CI (smoke). Due 2026-03-24.
- Ava: coordinate customer communication for resolved INF-2338 and prepare release note snippet. Due 2026-03-18 morning.

Blockers / risks:
- REL-1435 telemetry schema mismatch could break parts of observability if not migrated. High priority.
- Race condition REL-1430 in router causing transient grpc timeouts under a narrow traffic pattern. Mitigation in HOTFIX-21 but needs additional guard.
- Capacity: Dedicated pools fill to 95% for a key customer region during synthetic load tests — monitor dedicated pool utilization and consider pre-warming or temporary quota increase.

Decisions made:
- Delay full rollout of HOTFIX-21 until extended canary in us-east-1 completes and synthetic load looks stable.
- Proceed with v1.42 main window but gate step to ensure REL-1435 migration job completes first.

Notes / loose ends:
- Verify SLA telemetry is not impacted by telemetry schema change. Follow up with Product Analytics.
- Consider adding a small chaos step to canary (routing table rebuild during low traffic) to increase confidence. Design doc: REL-CANARY-CHAOS (linked in Confluence).

Next meeting:
- Weekly sync: 2026-03-24 15:00 PT (agenda: post-release review, HOTFIX-21 final status, autoscaler test results).

Raw standup snippets (collected):
- Maya: "canary looks stable in eu-west; will watch us-east during extended window; prepping notes for release notes."
- Carlos: "schema migration tests passed in staging; running read-only migration tonight."
- Priya: "observability panel in progress; will post PR by Fri."
- Ethan: "autoscaler stress harness is in repo; wiring into CI next week."

Attachments / references: see linked_artifacts above.

-- End notes --
